text:
sarah (support): Customer reports a spike of 5xxs and timeouts for hosted /v1/generate since 09:12 UTC. ~50% error rate on their traffic, p50 latency up to 600ms, p95 ~2.1s, a lot of 502/504. Customer is seeing request failures and billing spikes. Need triage :rotating_light:

alex (oncall-sre): I'm on it, creating warroom. Paging @rachel (eng-runtime) and @tony (eng-platform). Any quick mitigation suggestions?

incident-bot: Incident warroom created: #warroom-1758210001 (severity: customer-impact)

rachel (eng-runtime): Can you paste a sample failing request + response headers? Are they using streaming or normal sync calls? Any recent model changes for that endpoint?

priya (support): Customer is in eu-west-1 region, non-streaming usage. Auth returns 200, but backend returns 502 and then connection reset. No recent model pin from the customer side; they call our hosted endpoint with model=redwood-alpha-1.

sarah (support): Sample curl + response snippet: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","input":"...long prompt...","max_tokens":1024}'``` Response: ```HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway\nx-edge-request-id: abc-123\nbody: "upstream closed connection"```

alex (oncall-sre): No runtime deploys in last 2h. We did an autoscaler config rollout at 03:00 UTC but that targets dedicated clusters, not hosted. Could be a routing/backpressure issue. I'm going to enable a safety fallback route for that customer's traffic to a smaller model to reduce pressure.

tony (eng-platform): Recommend routing them to `redwood-alpha-1-quant-small` as a temporary fallback. I can push a routing rule for the customer id. Alex, can you confirm customer id and whether they have reserved capacity?

priya (support): Customer id: cust_78910. They are on standard hosted (no reserved). I'll inform them of the temporary fallback.

alex (oncall-sre): Applying routing override now -> `set-route cust_78910 -> redwood-alpha-1-quant-small` (done). Monitoring.

rachel (eng-runtime): While mitigation is in place, let's get logs and stack traces from the inference pods that served eu-west. Run `kubectl logs -l app=inference-runtime -n hosted --since=30m --tail=200` and check for `KVCache` stall or OOM entries. Also collect proxy (envoy) upstream timeouts.

sarah (support): Running quick grep shows repeated `upstream reset` and `504 downstream timeout` in envoy for a subset of backend pods.

rachel (eng-runtime): That points to backend worker saturation. Two follow-up asks: 1) capture `runtime/metrics` for the affected pods (open connections, queue length), 2) get one example request that reproduces with a short script so we can replay locally. Repro script suggestion: ```bash
# repro script
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-1","input":"<very long prompt to exercise KV cache>","max_tokens":1024}' https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate
```

alex (oncall-sre): After routing override, customer reports error rate dropped ~80% and p95 latency back to normal. Good mitigation.

maria (customer): Thanks — errors have decreased and most requests are succeeding now. But we still saw a billing spike during the window, can you help reconcile charges?

josh (product): We'll open a billing review and prepare a customer-facing summary. Action items: 1) eng-runtime to collect pod metrics + traces and confirm root cause (rachel), 2) eng-platform to audit recent autoscaler/config rollouts and routing policies (tony), 3) SRE to capture repro and run a load-replay to verify fix (alex), 4) Support to coordinate customer comms and billing review (priya + josh).

rachel (eng-runtime): Initial hypothesis: worker queue saturation from long-seq requests triggering KV cache memory pressure + proxy timeouts. We will instrument a deeper metric (kv_cache.misses, worker.queue_length) and run a controlled replay.

tony (eng-platform): I'll roll back the non-critical autoscaler flag if it's implicated and add a safeguard to not apply host-wide changes during peak hours.

priya (support): I'll send cust_78910 a note: "temporary fallback applied, errors reduced; we are investigating root cause and will follow up with billing reconciliation."

alex (oncall-sre): Closing the immediate warroom. We'll track the postmortem and a remediation plan. I'll create a postmortem doc and assign owners. Last note: if we see another spike, we should have an automated rollback to fallback-model route for affected customers.

josh (product): Postmortem owners: rachel (root cause), tony (config rollbacks and guardrails), alex (replay + monitoring), priya/josh (customer + billing). Timeline: draft postmortem in 48h, final in 7 days.

maria (customer): Appreciate the fast response. Please include the billing reconciliation in the follow-up.

sarah (support): Action items summarized in thread. I'll create a follow-up ticket for billing and link the postmortem when ready. :white_check_mark:
